topics.title: An Interesting Property
topics.text:
I was recently watching this video. I was curious to see if there were more numbers that could be expressed in the form $m^k-m$, where $m$ and $k$ are positive integers, in multiple ways. I ran a computer program, which gave me a few values.



Afterward, I saw this list. I was surprised to see only eight positive numbers are known which can be written in the form $m^k-m$ in multiple ways, with $m$ and $k$ being integers. They are $6$, $30$, $210$, $240$, $2184$, $8190$, $78120$, and $24299970$. As an example, $240 = 3^5-3 = 16^2-16$.



Here's the question: Are there infinitely many numbers with this property? According to the OEIS, the next term, if it exists would have to be greater than $2 \cdot 10^{17}$. It seems to me that there are infinitely many of them, but only eight are known. What are your thoughts?

topics.title: Pandigital Powers of 2
topics.text:
Hi Everyone,



I was recently investigating an interesting problem, and thought some of you may enjoy it.



For the purpose of this problem, define a pandigital number as any number that uses all the digits 0 - 9 at least once. In other words, repeating digits is allowed as long as every digit is used at least once.



The question is simple: What's the largest power of 2 that's not a pandigital number? You might think there are infinitely many of non-pandigital powers of two, and maybe that's true. Try to prove it if you think so. But I did a little investigation with Python, and found that for all the powers of two up to $2^{10000}$, the largest one that isn't pandigital is $2^{168}$, which doesn't use the digit $2$. In other words, $2^{n}$ is definitely a pandigital number for $169 \leq n \leq 10000$.



I think that all powers of $2$ larger than $2^{168}$ are pandigital, and $2^{168}$ is the largest one that isn't. Let me know if you don't think so!

1. A 6-8-10 right triangle is rotated about the side length 10 units. What is the volume of the resulting solid? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth.



2. An eight-digit number N has one 2, three 3s, two 4s, and two 5s as digits. If N can be expressed as a power of 2, what is the value of N?



3.Ty flips a fair coin 20 times. What is the probability that it lands heads up and tails up equal numbers of times? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest thousandth.
